text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes commonly co-occurs with other chronic conditions, known as comorbidities. These include hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, cardiovascular diseases (like heart disease and stroke), chronic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy, and even mental health conditions like depression.
snippet_highlighted_words: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, cardiovascular diseases (like heart disease and stroke), chronic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy, and even mental health conditions like depression

list.title: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD):
list.snippet: People with type 2 diabetes are at a significantly higher risk of developing heart disease, stroke, and other circulatory problems.

list.title: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure):
list.snippet: Hypertension is very common in people with type 2 diabetes and can further damage blood vessels and increase the risk of CVD.

list.title: Hyperlipidemia (High Cholesterol):
list.snippet: Abnormal levels of lipids (cholesterol and triglycerides) in the blood are frequent in type 2 diabetes and contribute to cardiovascular problems.

list.title: Obesity:
list.snippet: Obesity is a major risk factor for developing type 2 diabetes, and many individuals with type 2 diabetes are also obese.

list.title: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD):
list.snippet: Diabetes is a leading cause of CKD, which can progress to kidney failure if not managed.

list.title: Diabetic Retinopathy:
list.snippet: High blood sugar levels can damage blood vessels in the retina, leading to vision problems and potentially blindness.

list.title: Neuropathy (Nerve Damage):
list.snippet: Nerve damage, particularly in the feet, can cause pain, numbness, and increase the risk of foot ulcers and infections.

list.title: Depression:
list.snippet: People with type 2 diabetes are more likely to experience depression, and this can affect their ability to manage their diabetes.

list.title: Sleep Disorders:
list.snippet: Type 2 diabetes can disrupt sleep patterns, and sleep disorders like sleep apnea are more common in people with diabetes.

list.title: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease):
list.snippet: Individuals with type 2 diabetes may also have a higher risk of developing COPD.

list.title: Thyroid Disorders:
list.snippet: Type 2 diabetes can be associated with thyroid problems.

list.title: Increased Health Risks:
list.snippet: Comorbidities can significantly worsen the health outcomes of people with type 2 diabetes, leading to increased morbidity and mortality.

list.title: Impact on Self-Management:
list.snippet: The presence of multiple chronic conditions can make it more challenging for individuals to manage their diabetes, adhere to treatment plans, and maintain a healthy lifestyle.

list.title: Higher Healthcare Costs:
list.snippet: Managing multiple chronic conditions can be expensive, both for individuals and the healthcare system.

list.title: Reduced Quality of Life:
list.snippet: Comorbidities can negatively impact a person's physical and mental well-being, affecting their overall quality of life.

text_blocks.snippet: Understanding the potential comorbidities associated with type 2 diabetes is crucial for effective prevention, early diagnosis, and comprehensive management of the disease.
